clue.text: Baby-face may appear so flighty

parts.note: a chubby infant face looks like that of a winged angel child, and those angels can fly, hence flighty

explanation.surface: Someone with a baby face might come across as a bit giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' looks like it means giddy, but the cherubs of art have wings, so they are flighty in the sense of able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are painted as plump winged infants, so an innocent, round baby face is called angelic in that way.

clue.text: Gin, singularly, from the 3. nether regions

definitions.meaning: An old Dutch gin, here in the singular form

explanation.walkthrough: 'nether regions' suggests the underworld but means the Low Countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollands is a Dutch gin, and Holland is another name for the Netherlands, the nether regions read as low lands.

clue.text: We may hear worse, anyhow, of this entertainment

indicators.note: anyhow means in any order at all, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking the audience about a show they found worse than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: A RAREE-SHOW is an old peep show carried around in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a street peep show, a travelling kind of popular show.

clue.text: Brown boy astride a bay

indicators.note: the boy sits with legs either side of the colour

parts.note: tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A boy riding a bay horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like a horse colour; it is Botany Bay, in Sydney, where Captain Cook landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany Bay is an inlet in Sydney named for its plants, so the word names a bay.

clue.text: Avian airy. Utopia

parts.note: the ideal city built in the sky by the birds in Aristophanes' play The Birds

explanation.surface: A bird's ideal world up in the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase translates Nephelokokkygia, the birds' city in Aristophanes; it now means a fanciful dream world.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the birds' city in the air from a Greek comedy, and now any impractical fantasy realm.

clue.text: Making a crafty bob when in debt, as Barabbas did

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for debt

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red, so debt gives RED

indicators.note: crafty suggests cunning rearrangement, so the three letters of bob are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone in debt makes a cunning shilling, just as the biblical prisoner did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crafty' scrambles BOB to OBB, which goes inside RED. A bob is an old British shilling. Barabbas, released instead of Jesus, is called a robber in John's Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Barabbas is described in the Gospel of John as a robber, so what he did was steal.

clue.text: Engineer stands-but not his, ground

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
to stand someone a drink treats them

explanation.surface: The engineer holds firm, but not on his position.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps. 'stands' is used as in 'stands a round'; the surface sense of holding ground leads into the definition: he does not stand his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: One who withdraws or falls back gives up ground rather than holding it.

clue.text: Swimming the Hellespont such a poetic feat

definitions.text: Swimming the Hellespont such a poetic feat

parts.words: Swimming the Hellespont such a poetic feat
parts.note: the poet Lord Byron swam the Dardanelles in 1810, so the feat is named after him

explanation.surface: Swimming across the Hellespont was a deed worthy of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Byron swam the Hellespont (the Dardanelles) in imitation of Leander.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to Lord Byron, the poet who made that swim.

clue.text: House-painter's ill-humour ?

definitions.meaning: a water-based paint for walls is what a house-painter uses
an old sense of bad temper or disordered mood

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a water-based wall paint and, in older usage, a disordered temper; it is also a dog disease.

clue.text: One providing punch may also tap this wine

definitions.text: One providing punch may also tap this
definitions.meaning: in old boxing slang blood is called ..., and a boxer landing a punch may draw it, tapping it like a cask

explanation.walkthrough: Punch is also a drink made with wine, which sends the solver towards a punch bowl, but the punch here is a boxer's blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is red Bordeaux wine, and old boxing slang uses the same name for blood drawn by a punch.

clue.text: It may cause us to draw from the centre

indicators.note: the clue says something causes the letters of us to draw to come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A force pulls people away from the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It may cause' signals that the letters of US TO DRAW are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving from the centre is moving away towards the outside, the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Heed point taken by Edward " when on one's beam-ends ?

indicators.note: the point is followed by the name, as if Edward took it along

parts.note: to heed is to care
a point of the compass, E for east
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Pay attention to the point Edward made when you were at the end of your tether.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship on her beam-ends is lying over on her side, which is what careening a ship does to clean the hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel careened has been heeled over on its side, exactly the state of lying on its beam-ends.

clue.text: Show girl goes round in 100

indicators.note: the girl's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A showgirl does a circuit in a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display it openly, a synonym of show as a verb.

clue.text: State that goes back oh, to the start of our era!

indicators.note: the clue says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the first year of the Christian era is AD 1, written AD I

explanation.surface: A state whose history reaches right back to year one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns OH + AD I into I DA HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the north-west, famous for potatoes.

clue.text: Immediately suggests a lightning coronation?.:

definitions.meaning: split as ..., an instant queen, ER being the royal cipher

explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at once; split up, it reads as an instant monarch, ER being the royal cipher.

clue.text: Flower of bumboat women.

parts.note: a meadow flower shares its name with the bumboat woman of Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, whom she might call the pick of her trade

explanation.surface: The finest of the women selling goods from small boats.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore, Little Buttercup is the bumboat woman who sells provisions to sailors; 'flower' also means the finest of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow meadow flower is also the name of the Pinafore character, the best-known bumboat woman.

clue.text: Last, liner after repair put back in position

indicators.note: after repair means after the letters are fixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A ship returned to her berth after repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after repair' rearranges LAST LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: To install again is to put something back where it belongs.

clue.text: Music-maker could drop: in for 9

indicators.note: drop here means drop into, so the word in goes into the other

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, a red wine

explanation.surface: An instrument that might be dropped for a glass of red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' puts IN into CLARET, the answer to 9 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument is something that makes music.

clue.text: Now AA fire in the South-east for 'a Christmas visitor ?.

indicators.note: the other letters go inside those for the South-east

parts.note: SE abbreviates south-east
taken as written
anti-aircraft fire is flak

explanation.surface: An air-raid in the South-east of England heralds a seasonal guest.
explanation.walkthrough: AA here is anti-aircraft, not the motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling ice crystal is a welcome seasonal arrival at a white Christmas.

clue.text: Objects to attitudes taken after work

indicators.note: the attitudes come after the work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
poses are attitudes struck

explanation.surface: Someone resents attitudes adopted after the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to resist or stand against it.

clue.text: Scholar who takes our measure, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken and heard rather than spelt

parts.note: one who measures size is a sizer

explanation.surface: A scholar who weighs us up.
explanation.walkthrough: A SIZAR is an undergraduate at Cambridge or Trinity College Dublin receiving help with costs.
explanation.definitionFit: At certain universities, this is a student on reduced fees, historically doing duties in return.

clue.text: He loves-raising capital for Italians, it's odd

indicators.note: in a down clue raising reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name of Rome

indicators.note: odd suggests strange, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: He adores raising money for Italians, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' reverses ROMA to AMOR; 'odd' rearranges ITS to IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover, one devoted to romance, is someone who loves.

clue.text: Southern shooting 'game leads to fights

parts.note: craps is a dice game, in which you shoot the dice

explanation.surface: A Southern dice game turns into brawls.
explanation.walkthrough: Dice players 'shoot' the dice at craps, so this is no gun game.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps are informal brawls or squabbles.

clue.text: "An — ether, a diviner air" (Wordsworth)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank line from Wordsworth's poem Laodamia, where the missing word means more spacious

explanation.surface: A quotation from Wordsworth with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Laodamia: the missing comparative pairs with diviner.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the comparative of a word meaning plentiful or spacious, matching diviner in the next phrase.

clue.text: Cocoa's in order for a TT one

indicators.note: putting the letters in order rearranges them

explanation.surface: Ordering cocoa for a teetotal event.
explanation.walkthrough: TT reads as teetotal, but it is the Isle of Man TT motorcycle races, a famous event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tourist Trophy races are a sporting event, a kind of special happening.

clue.text: Van Diemen's'home for the devil

definitions.meaning: Van Diemen's Land was the old name of the island
the island is where the ... devil, a marsupial, lives in the wild

explanation.walkthrough: The devil is not Satan but the carnivorous marsupial found only on that island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian island state was first named Van Diemen's Land and is the native habitat of the Tasmanian devil.

clue.text: A Visigoth in the 'style of a mollified Lionheart

parts.note: the French a la means in the style of

indicators.note: mollified means softened, so the hard part is taken away

parts.note: Richard the Lionheart, King Richard I

explanation.surface: A Gothic warrior who resembled a softened crusader king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mollified' removes HARD from RICHARD, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaric I was the Visigothic king who sacked Rome in 410.

clue.text: Take umbrage at being given second' errand

definitions.meaning: sent again, ..., as someone given a second errand is

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-SENT, sent a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be offended by something is to feel bitter about it; and someone sent off once more is sent again.

clue.text: Notes thus overdue make us forlorn

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
so means thus
late means overdue

explanation.surface: Overdue bills leave us feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn and bleak both describe a lonely, abandoned sadness.
